check_events.statement: For an arbitrary scheme over Qbar, every absolute scheme automorphism induces an automorphism of its chosen Qbar of constants.
check_events.place: Opening definition and sequence (1), without the added right-margin hypothesis
check_events.outcome: Take X=Spec(Qbar×Qbar), with the diagonal Qbar structure, and the absolute automorphism induced by (a,b)↦(conjugate(a),b). It sends the diagonal element (i,i) to (−i,i), which is not diagonal. Thus arbitrary absolute automorphisms need not preserve the specified Qbar structure; the unqualified restriction map is not generally defined. This is a check of the unqualified statement, not a change to the ink. Refined statement ID: 143_scan002_S01_intrinsic_constants.

check_events.statement: If the specified Qbar is exactly the integral closure of Q in the relevant ring of global functions, absolute automorphisms preserve it and the kernel of restriction is Aut(X/Qbar).
check_events.place: Right marginal Il faut supposer note and sequence (1)
check_events.outcome: An absolute scheme automorphism fixes rational scalars in its Q-algebra of global functions. It preserves the property of satisfying a monic polynomial with rational coefficients, hence preserves the specified integral closure Qbar. Using the inverse-pullback convention for the group law, restriction then gives a group homomorphism to Gal(Qbar/Q); its kernel consists exactly of automorphisms preserving the Qbar structure. This checks the displayed initial sequence under the written intrinsic-constants hypothesis, without asserting surjectivity onto Gamma.

check_events.statement: For a subfield K of Qbar containing Q, its closed fixing subgroup Gamma_K has finite index precisely when K/Q is finite.
check_events.place: Paragraph (3), parenthesis d’indice fini ssi K fini sur Q
check_events.outcome: For finite K=Q(alpha), characteristic zero makes the minimal polynomial separable and the Gamma-orbit of alpha has [K:Q] elements; its stabilizer is Gamma_K, so [Gamma:Gamma_K]=[K:Q]. If K were infinite but its finite subextensions had bounded degrees, choose one of maximal degree: adjoining any further element would not increase that degree, forcing K to equal it, a contradiction. Thus an infinite K has finite subextensions of unbounded degree, and their stabilizer indices bound [Gamma:Gamma_K] below without bound.
